solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Group of companies against developing tourism

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: developing means taking a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A business group objects to the growth of the tourist trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' looks like part of the surface's objection, but it simply gives CON, as in pros and cons; 'developing' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A consortium is an association of several businesses working together on a venture.

clue.text: Reject unfashionable actors

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
the cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a troupe of performers as no longer in vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun sense: an outcast is a person rejected by society.

clue.text: Senior citizen following second TV serial

indicators.note: following says the pensioner comes after the abbreviation for second

parts.note: OAP stands for old-age pensioner, the British term for a senior citizen

explanation.surface: A pensioner watches a television drama straight after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running television drama serial.

clue.text: Meat from zebra she recommended

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone was advised by a woman to eat zebra meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' picks the letters out of zebRA SHE Recommended.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasher is a thin slice of bacon, a kind of meat.

clue.text: Imply rigour on regular basis is of poor quality

parts.note: to infer is loosely used for to imply or suggest

indicators.note: on a regular basis means taking every other letter of the word rigour

explanation.surface: Suggesting that routine strictness yields shoddy results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on regular basis' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of RIGOUR: IOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferior describes something lower in standard, second-rate.

clue.text: Dark spirit rising over Kentucky?

indicators.note: over says the first part sits above the second in this down entry
in a down clue, rising means the word for the spirit reads upwards

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane
KY is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Kentucky

explanation.surface: A shadowy drink climbing above the American state — perhaps bourbon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns RUM into MUR, placed 'over' KY.
explanation.definitionFit: Murky means gloomy and obscure, lacking light.

clue.text: Bleep a lord in broadcast? Very bad!

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A censor bleeps out a peer's swearing on air — shocking!
explanation.definitionFit: Deplorable means deserving strong condemnation, truly dreadful.

clue.text: Stop filming girl's outdated weapon

parts.note: a director calls cut to stop the filming
a lass is a girl, the 's reading as is

explanation.surface: A director halts the shoot because the actress's sword is anachronistic.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword once used by sailors, no longer in service.

clue.text: Male on island in breakfast food ritual

indicators.note: in places the male, on and island letters inside the breakfast food

parts.note: cereal is a typical breakfast food

explanation.surface: A man on an island eats his breakfast cereal as a daily routine.
explanation.walkthrough: M, ON and I go into CERE-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective ceremonial means relating to ritual or formal occasions.

clue.text: Supporting Church power

parts.note: for means in favour of, supporting
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Backing the Church's authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Force and power are synonyms for strength or might.

clue.text: Genuine religious teaching attracts a learner

indicators.note: attracts says the teaching draws the following letters to itself

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: Authentic religious instruction draws in a new student.
explanation.definitionFit: Real and genuine are synonyms, both meaning authentic.

clue.text: British and French fish — a large shopping?

parts.note: et is French for and
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Buying a big fish in Britain and France on a shopping trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shopping' here is British slang for informing on someone, not buying goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopping in British slang means informing on someone to the police, an act of treachery.

clue.text: Challenging attitude of French man due to wed

parts.note: de is French for of
a fiance is a man engaged to be married

explanation.surface: A Frenchman about to marry has a combative stance.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance, a bold disposition that challenges authority.

clue.text: Topic monarch finds dull to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with says the dull word comes first, before the monarch

parts.note: matt describes a dull, non-glossy finish
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A king finds the subject tedious at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter is a subject or issue under discussion.

clue.text: One-time rural dweller's area becomes old

indicators.note: becomes says one letter of the dweller is swapped for another

parts.note: a farmer is a country dweller

explanation.surface: A country person's land has aged with time.
explanation.definitionFit: Former and one-time both mean previous, having held a role in the past.

clue.text: Check car going around Northern Ireland

indicators.note: going around means the car word encloses the next letters

parts.note: motor is an informal word for a car

explanation.surface: Inspecting a car as it drives round Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor is to observe and check progress over time; a verb sense.

clue.text: Tenant perhaps not so effusive after vacation

parts.note: less means not so much

indicators.note: after vacation means once the inside of the word effusive is emptied, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A renter grows calmer once the holiday is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after vacation' empties EFFUSIVE to EE, so the word is about emptying, not holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds a lease, and a tenant is one example; hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Eileen, getting disheartened, changed peignoir

indicators.note: changed means these letters are shuffled into a new order
disheartened means the heart of the word getting is removed, keeping its outer letters

explanation.surface: Eileen, feeling low, slips into her dressing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves GG from GETTING; 'changed' rearranges EILEEN plus GG.
explanation.definitionFit: A peignoir is a woman's light dressing gown, much like a negligee.

clue.text: Metal framework impressive, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for impressive is taken by its sound

parts.note: great means impressive

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a metal structure is magnificent.
explanation.definitionFit: A grate is a metal frame holding fuel in a fireplace.

clue.text: Spurn cakes brought around

indicators.note: brought around means the word for the cakes is turned to face the other way

parts.note: buns are small cakes

explanation.surface: Refusing the pastries that were handed round.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub is to rebuff or ignore someone pointedly.

clue.text: Initially felt envious at the achievement

indicators.note: initially means taking the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: At first someone was jealous of another's success.
explanation.definitionFit: A feat is a notable accomplishment requiring skill or courage.

clue.text: Once more making a profit

parts.note: a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Turning a profit for a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means one more time, repeatedly.

clue.text: Cover PM visiting Home Counties

indicators.note: visiting puts the prime minister inside the region letters

parts.note: SE stands for south-east, the region of England where the Home Counties, those around London, lie
Edward Heath was a British prime minister

explanation.surface: Covering up a prime minister's trip to the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: HEATH is Ted Heath, UK prime minister 1970-74.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe is to put a blade into a cover, or to encase.

clue.text: Simple elm tree? Nay, complex!

indicators.note: complex means intricate and tangled, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests that identifying an elm tree is not easy but complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means basic and straightforward, as in Holmes's 'Elementary, my dear Watson'.
